name: VALUE
question: Does adding multichannel urodynamics to an office evaluation improve outcomes after surgery for uncomplicated, demonstrable stress-predominant urinary incontinence?

design.blinding: Outcome assessors blinded; surgeons and participants unblinded

arms.label: Office evaluation plus urodynamic testing before planned continence surgery
office evaluation alone before planned continence surgery

design.population: Women aged 21 years or older with uncomplicated, demonstrable stress-predominant urinary incontinence seeking surgery; positive office stress test, postvoid residual below 150 mL, and no urinary infection.

verdictNote: Office evaluation met the 11-percentage-point noninferiority margin in the per-protocol analysis.
takeaway: Before surgery for uncomplicated, demonstrable stress-predominant incontinence, office evaluation alone was noninferior to office evaluation plus multichannel urodynamics for 12-month patient-reported treatment success: 200/259 (77.2%) versus 203/264 (76.9%), with an 11-percentage-point prespecified margin.

reports.label: Primary 12-month report
reports.citation: Nager CW, Brubaker L, Litman HJ, et al. "A Randomized Trial of Urodynamic Testing before Stress-Incontinence Surgery." *N Engl J Med.* 2012;366(21):1987-1997. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1113595

results.measure: 12-month patient-reported composite success; risk difference in percentage points (urodynamics minus office only)
results.note: Per-protocol analysis included 523/630 randomized women. Success required at least 70% reduction in Urogenital Distress Inventory score and 'much better' or 'very much better' on Patient Global Impression of Improvement. The upper CI bound for urodynamics minus office only was below the prespecified 11-point margin.
results.locator: Author-manuscript PDF pp3-5, Outcomes and Primary Outcome; Fig 2

results.measure: 12-month composite success plus negative standardized 300-mL stress test among surgically treated women with available stress-test data
results.note: Planned surgical subgroup analysis; only 443 of 586 surgically treated women had follow-up stress-test data.
results.locator: Author-manuscript PDF pp3,5, Planned Subgroup Analysis and Success of Surgical Treatment

harms.label: Any adverse event
harms.locator: Author-manuscript PDF p5, Primary Outcome; Supplementary Appendix Table 7 cited there
harms.note: P=0.55; main article reports percentages without event counts. Events assessed after surgery, at discharge, and at 3 and 12 months; no significant difference in voiding dysfunction was reported.

delivery.label: Assigned preoperative evaluation
delivery.value: Office evaluation included provocative stress test, postvoid residual, urinalysis or culture, and urethral-mobility assessment. Added urodynamics comprised noninstrumented uroflowmetry, filling cystometry with Valsalva leak-point pressures, and pressure-flow study; urethral pressure profilometry or video was optional by site practice.
delivery.locator: Author-manuscript PDF pp2-3, Study Design and Procedures

delivery.label: Surgery received
delivery.locator: Author-manuscript PDF p5, Success of Surgical Treatment
delivery.note: Among the 17 without surgery after added urodynamics, 10 canceled, 4 changed to nonsurgical treatment and 3 had medical contraindications; P=0.12 for the between-arm comparison.

delivery.label: Operative mix
delivery.locator: Author-manuscript PDF p6, Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment; Supplementary Appendix Table 8 cited there
delivery.note: The balance included mini-slings, traditional slings, retropubic urethropexy and urethral-bulking injection; the main report gives percentages without procedure counts.

reports.followUpLocator: Author-manuscript PDF pp3-5, Outcomes and Primary Outcome

reports.label: Diagnosis and treatment-plan analysis
reports.citation: Sirls LT, Richter HE, Litman HJ, et al. "The Effect of Urodynamic Testing on Clinical Diagnosis, Treatment Plan and Outcomes in Women Undergoing Stress Urinary Incontinence Surgery." *J Urol.* 2013;189(1):204-209. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.09.050
reports.followUp: Treatment plans after preoperative testing and outcomes at 12 months

results.measure: Within the urodynamic-testing arm, changed diagnosis after office assessment
results.note: Overactive-bladder and suspected intrinsic-sphincter-deficiency diagnoses fell, while voiding-dysfunction diagnoses rose.
results.locator: PMC full text, Results: Diagnoses and Table 1

results.measure: Within the urodynamic-testing arm, any global plan change
results.note: Changes could include procedure, planned sling tension or added nonsurgical therapy; observational comparison within one randomized arm.
results.locator: PMC full text, Results: Treatment, paragraph after Table 2

results.measure: Association of urodynamics-driven plan change with 12-month treatment success; odds ratio
results.note: Within-arm observational analysis; the interval includes substantial benefit and harm.
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract: Results and Results: Outcomes

results.endpoint: Postoperative urgency-incontinence treatment after plan change
results.measure: Association of urodynamics-driven plan change with postoperative urgency-incontinence treatment; odds ratio
results.note: Within-arm observational association, not a randomized comparison; the endpoint counted treatment at 3 or 12 months.
results.locator: PMC full text, Abstract: Results and Discussion

delivery.label: Specific surgical-plan changes after urodynamics
delivery.value: Surgery canceled in 4/294 (1.4%); procedure changed in 16/294 (5.4%), including 13/294 (4.4%) switches between retropubic and transobturator midurethral slings; a sling-tension modification was planned for 20/294 (6.8%) but performed in 7/20.
delivery.locator: PMC full text, Results: Treatment and Table 2
delivery.note: These are within-arm changes; they do not represent a randomized difference in the distribution of operations.
